en.headline: Building maintenance council to receive HK$413 million and hire 160 staff
en.dek: The Development Bureau said the new body will complete registration next month and focus subsidies on 80 percent of older private buildings after the Tai Po fire.
body: The Development Bureau has proposed allocating HK$413 million to the planned Building Maintenance Support and Services Council, which will take over and expand support for owners of ageing buildings following the Wang Fuk Court fire in Tai Po.

In a paper to the Legislative Council, the bureau said the sum includes HK$100 million in start-up capital, funds previously earmarked for Urban Renewal Authority services, and the remaining balance from the Smart Tender scheme. Subsidies will target owners of lower-rateable-value buildings, covering about 80 percent of private residential and composite blocks aged 30 years or more.

The non-statutory company, wholly owned by the government, is expected to complete registration and board appointments within the next month. It will prioritise roughly 1,800 pending projects that have not yet appointed contractors, assign inspection consultants, handle tendering and bid evaluation, and monitor supervision consultants. The bureau said the council aims to hire about 160 staff, including professionals and case managers, with recruitment already under way.

zh.headline: 樓宇維修支援及服務局獲撥4.13億元 擬聘160人
zh.dek: 發展局表示新機構下月完成註冊，資助將集中於八成樓齡30年或以上私樓，因應大埔宏福苑大火後改革。
body: 發展局建議向擬成立的樓宇維修支援及服務局撥款4.13億元，以接管並加強對舊樓業主的支援，回應大埔宏福苑大火後的改革需要。
局方向立法會提交的文件指出，款項包括1億元起動資金、原預留予市建局服務的撥款，以及「招標妥」計劃的餘額。資助將聚焦應課差餉租值較低的樓宇業主，涵蓋全港約八成樓齡30年或以上的私人住宅及綜合用途樓宇。
這間由政府全資擁有的非法定公司預期下月內完成公司註冊及董事局委任，並優先處理約1800個尚未委聘承建商的工程。服務包括指派驗樓顧問、代辦招標及評標，以及監察監督顧問表現。發展局表示，機構初期計劃招聘約160名員工，包括專業及個案管理人員，招聘工作已經展開。
